study: Greenaway-McGrevy & Phillips (2023) JUE 136:103555, Auckland upzoning & construction
comparison_design: Multi-period DiD (event-study) + partial/set identification of counterfactual (Rambachan-Roth style) to bound spillovers
comparison_group_definition: Non-upzoned residential land (mainly Single House zone and residential parcels whose FAR did not rise) within same suburb, vs upzoned THA/MHU/MHS land (~75% of residential land). Excluded Large Lot and Rural & Coastal Settlement zones, Hauraki Gulf islands, and pre-2017 Special Housing Area permits.
similarity_covariates: No matching. Suburb-zone FE absorb levels. For spillover mechanism: Manhattan distance to CBD, distance to nearest highway onramp, undeveloped residential land area, zoning concentration. Robustness controls: floorspace, building age, garages, distance to CBD/onramp/rapid-transit station.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: y_ijt = alpha_ij (suburb x zone-type FE) + phi_s (period FE) + sum beta_s 1{s=t, upzoned}; robustness replaces common period FE with SA-specific period effects (neighbourhood-specific trends). Counterfactual set: extrapolate control-group pre-trend linearly and allow deviation M*t/T (main M=14, ~4x extrapolated trend) to absorb displacement from controls.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Event-study pre-coefficients flat ('no apparent trend prior to treatment'); App. A3 structural-break test: significant post-2015 trend reduction only in control group; land-price and sales-volume placebo with 2012 date show no differential pre-trends.
unit_of_analysis: Suburb (SA) x zone-type cell by year; 479 Statistical Areas; annual 2010-2021
outcome_variable: Number of new dwellings in building consents (permits), split attached vs detached; extensions excluded
outcome_standardization: Levels (not logs) so counterfactual bounds can be built; results aggregated to city totals and expressed as % of dwelling stock (~4.1%); completions approximated with 95%/99% conversion rates. No per-capita scaling.
treatment_definition_and_dose: Binary: upzoned if zone FAR (storey limit x site coverage ratio, computed for ~115 legacy residential zones across 7 former councils) rose under AUP. Heterogeneity by destination zone (THA, MHU, MHS).
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Draft AUP March 2013, notified Sept 2013 (interim build-to-PAUP), operative Nov 2016. Treatment dated 2015 = pre-intervention peak of control permits (conservative, captures anticipation). Alternatives 2013/2014/2016.
spillover_handling: Core feature: displacement from control to treated areas would inflate DiD; handled by set identification bounding control trend (M parameter) without assuming spillovers decay with distance. Mechanism regressions show spillover tied to undeveloped (greenfield) land in controls.
inference_method: SEs clustered by SA; fixed-length confidence intervals (FLCI) per Rambachan-Roth for bounded sets; Newey-West panel SEs (bandwidth 2) for control-trend break test.
robustness_checks: Alternative treatment dates 2013/14/16; alternative treatment/control delineations (THA/MHU/MHS vs SH only; excluding downzoned areas; including SpHA permits); SA-specific period FE; zone-by-zone effects; sales volume and land-price analyses.
data_construction_and_cleaning: Consents geocoded (lat/long) and overlaid on pre- and post-AUP planning maps; missing coordinates repaired by nearest parcel (<2% of sample); dwelling counts summed by SA-year. No demolition data (demolition permits only for >3-storey), so figures are gross.
stated_limitations: Counterfactual depends on extrapolated linear trend specification ('point estimates will be sensitive'); allocation of spillovers across zones uses baseline construction weights; permits still trending up in 2021 so full effect unknown; permits not completions; gross not net of demolitions.
where_in_paper: Sec 2-3 (data, zoning, p4-6), Eq.1 p6, Sec 4 (p7-13), App A2-A5 (p17-18)

study: Greenaway-McGrevy (2026) Econ Modelling 160:107592, Auckland synthetic control
comparison_design: Synthetic control (Abadie-style, demeaned / Ferman-Pinto fixed-effects SC)
comparison_group_definition: Donor pool = other New Zealand Functional Urban Areas (commuting-zone based urban areas; 53 FUAs incl. Auckland). Excluded Christchurch (2011 earthquake idiosyncratic shock) and Warkworth (inside Auckland Council jurisdiction). NOTE: units are FUAs, not regions; TA-level and Australian-state donor variants in robustness.
similarity_covariates: Baseline: pre-treatment outcomes only (all years 1991-2015). Covariate variant: population growth, household income growth, dwellings growth (log differences at census years 1991/96/01/06/13).
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Nested Abadie optimisation: W on simplex minimising ||X1-X0W||_V; V chosen by CMA-ES (stochastic optimiser) to minimise pre-period RMSPE. Outcomes demeaned by subtracting each unit's pre-treatment average (equivalent to FE-SC; allows matching changes not levels).
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Weights: Tauranga 0.573, Kapiti Coast 0.213, Wellington 0.111, Hamilton 0.102. Visual fit good except early-2000s (4 consecutive years above synthetic; max abs gap 2.8 in 2002). Backdating test with 2010 placebo date.
unit_of_analysis: Functional Urban Area x year, annual 1991-2023
outcome_variable: New dwelling permits (consents)
outcome_standardization: Permits per 1,000 residents ('permitting rate'), June population estimates; pre-1996 population backcast/interpolated from 1991-96 census growth; demeaned. Also 3-yr moving-average smoothing variant. Cumulative excess permits expressed as % of total permits (46%).
treatment_definition_and_dose: Binary city-wide reform (AUP upzoned ~3/4 of residential land).
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Main date 2016 (AUP operative Nov 2016); alt 2013 (Housing Accord allowed PAUP rules from Sept 2013); in-time placebo 2010.
spillover_handling: Ran SC for each major donor (Tauranga, Hamilton) with Auckland reform as 'intervention' to test for displacement/positive spillovers: no persistent deviation; population growth in donors not reduced before 2020.
inference_method: Rank permutation (placebo-in-space) on post/pre RMSE ratios; new one-sided 'Positive Error RMSE ratio'; Auckland ranks 1/51, p=0.02.
robustness_checks: Leave-one-out donors; drop Hamilton+Tauranga (46.6%) or Wellington+Kapiti (42.3%); alt dates 2013 (47.5-50.5%) and 2010 backdate; 3-yr MA smoothing; Territorial-Authority units instead of FUAs (49.2%); add 5 Australian states to donor pool (little weight).
data_construction_and_cleaning: Stats NZ consents and population by urban area 1991-2023; census covariates; notes completion rates >90% via CCC data.
stated_limitations: Permits not completions; no intercensal dwelling stock; no demolition records; covariate inclusion can worsen outcome fit vs omitting covariates biases SC; SC overestimates Auckland dwelling growth, possible bias.
where_in_paper: Sec 3 data (p9-11), Sec 4.1 method (p17), Table 1 p18, Fig 6 p19, Sec 4.2-4.4 (p22-37)

study: Greenaway-McGrevy, Pacheco & Sorensen (2021) Urban Studies 58(5), Auckland upzoning & redevelopment premium
comparison_design: Repeat-sales hedonic difference-in-differences with zone x intensity interaction (pre vs post AUP)
comparison_group_definition: Properties in AUP Single House zone (least permissive; 25.5% of sample) as quasi-control vs Mixed Housing Suburban, Mixed Housing Urban, Terrace Housing & Apartments (treated). Pre-AUP zoning of each house not used.
similarity_covariates: Hedonic controls: log land area, log floor area, 2+ storey dummy, bedrooms, bathrooms, building age, log distance to CBD, log median household income. Key moderator: intensity ratio = improvement value / total assessed value (1 - LV/AV), a proxy for teardown opportunity cost.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Repeat-sales differencing removes time-invariant property effects; annualised log price change regressed on zone dummies, intensity, zone x intensity, and time-invariant hedonic controls. No area-unit FE in main model.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Placebo pre/post windows entirely before March 2013 draft AUP (three pairs): zone x intensity terms mostly insignificant (no anticipation of which areas upzoned). Intensity-ratio means similar across zones (0.41-0.45); population-density distributions similar across zones.
unit_of_analysis: Property (repeat-sale pair); n=2,340 (3,695 expanded)
outcome_variable: Log sale price (chattels removed); annualised appreciation between pre and post sale
outcome_standardization: Annualised % change in price (log difference / years between sales, mean gap 5.64 yrs).
treatment_definition_and_dose: Binary by destination zone (3 upzoned zones vs SH), plus interaction with continuous intensity ratio; redevelopment premium = coefficient on intensity; upzoning effect on premium = zone x intensity.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Pre sales 2010-2012 (before draft AUP March 2013); post sales Sept 2016-Dec 2017 (after Aug 2016 decisions version). Alternative windows tested.
inference_method: Conley (1999) spatial HAC SEs, 10 km radius, triangular kernel.
robustness_checks: Alternative pre/post windows (2007-09, 2007-12, 2014-17 post); expanded sample incl. non-exclusive land ownership (apartments, cross-leases).
data_construction_and_cleaning: CoreLogic NZ sales 2010-2017 with assessed land/improvement values; lat/long matched to ~133k AUP polygons; ~5% on polygon boundaries and 40% on road frontage repaired by nearest residential zone within 1.11 m; dropped vacant, leasehold, non-exclusive ownership, floor area <10 or >500 m2, land >10 ha, coverage >1, multiple sales in a quarter, missing.
stated_limitations: Pre-AUP zoning not controlled (THA areas may already have permitted density, attenuating estimates).

study: Maltman & Greenaway-McGrevy (2025) JHE 67:102032, Lower Hutt upzoning
comparison_design: Synthetic control for single treated TA (demeaned), plus SCs for neighbouring TAs to quantify displacement
comparison_group_definition: Donor pool = NZ Territorial Authorities (59 in published version) excluding Auckland (same intervention 2016), Christchurch (earthquake), Chatham Islands (tiny/remote) and the four other Wellington-region TAs (Wellington City, Upper Hutt, Porirua, Kapiti Coast) to avoid spillover contamination.
similarity_covariates: Main: outcome in every pre-treatment year 1996-2017. Alternative: intercensal population growth, intercensal income growth, dwellings per capita, Stats NZ projected population growth to 2040, and outcome in census years + 2017.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Abadie W on simplex minimising ||X1-X0W||_V, V chosen to minimise pre-period RMSPE; outcomes demeaned by pre-treatment average (Ferman-Pinto 2021 rationale citing Abadie 2021).
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Visual fit close 1996-2017 (no numeric RMSPE reported). Weights: Timaru 0.583, Wairoa 0.158, Opotiki 0.088, Waipa 0.075, Tasman 0.070, Selwyn 0.003; alt spec South Waikato 0.513, Tasman 0.204.
unit_of_analysis: Territorial Authority x year, annual (monthly aggregated because monthly noise impairs SC)
outcome_variable: Consents for new dwellings; by type (houses, townhouses, apartments, retirement units); population; hedonic rent index (published version)
outcome_standardization: Consents per 1,000 residents, demeaned; robustness with raw counts, pre-mean-normalised, and log-normalised consents (effects 2,950-3,274 units, all rank 1). Rents: hedonic rental index (MHUD new-tenancy bonds, double imputation), 2017=1.
treatment_definition_and_dose: Binary: Plan Change 43 (medium-density, notified Nov 2017); related PC39 (parking), parking minimum removal 2020, PC56 (MDRS 2022-23) treated as part of reform sequence.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Treatment year 2018 = first full year after PC43 notification (Abadie: first period outcome can react); robustness 2020 (partially operative) gives smaller effect (51.8% vs 66%). Notes concurrent fee waiver (2012-18) would bias toward underestimate.
spillover_handling: Separate SCs for each other Wellington-region TA (and pooled) with Lower Hutt reform as intervention; none significant; point-estimate deficits (921 or 1,488 units) subtracted to give regional net +12-17% (abstract of published: 10-18%).
inference_method: Placebo-in-space permutation with one-sided 'positive-error' MSPE ratio; rank 1/60, p=0.017; two-sided for spillover TAs.
robustness_checks: Leave-one-out donors; alt treatment date 2020; outcome transformations; population-growth SC to rule out COVID in-migration shock; covariate-based alternative predictor set.
data_construction_and_cleaning: Stats NZ monthly consents aggregated to annual 1990-2023; subnational population from 1996 (limits pre-period); rents from MHUD tenancy bond data via Greenaway-McGrevy & So (2024) hedonic index.
stated_limitations: Consents not completions (Stats NZ does not track completions; CCC proxy ~91%); hard to decompose effect across overlapping plan changes; gradual implementation; population denominator limits pre-period.
where_in_paper: WP 018: Sec 2.2, 3.2-3.4 (p12-15), Table 1 p17, Sec 4.1-4.3 (p18-26), Sec 5 (p27-34); published JHE Sec 6 (rents)

study: Anagol, Ferreira & Rexer (2026) AEJ:Policy 18(3), Sao Paulo zoning reform
comparison_design: Spatial regression discontinuity at treatment/control block boundaries (cross-section of post-period outcomes and RD-in-time event study), fuzzy-RD/IV scaling by change in max BAR (FAR), plus structural supply/demand model
comparison_group_definition: Control = blocks whose max building-to-area ratio (BAR) did not rise (or fell) under 2016 zoning; running variable = signed km distance to nearest block of the other group. Main spec uses all data (no bandwidth restriction).
similarity_covariates: Balance on pre-reform block covariates: density, land/construction value, building counts, residential/commercial share, employment, wages, firm counts (1 of 12 significant at 10%). Acknowledge treated blocks had lower pre-reform max BAR.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: RD: y = beta*1{x>0} + f(x) (linear/quadratic/cubic polynomial, interacted with side) + subprefeitura FE. First stage: ~1.4-point jump in max BAR at boundary; IV scales reduced form per 1 unit BAR. CCT optimal-bandwidth (~95 m, triangular kernel) as robustness.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Covariate balance tables/figures (App. A9-A10, Table A1); RD-by-half-year event study: pre-reform estimates insignificant.
unit_of_analysis: City block x quarter (3.2M block-quarter obs; ~45k blocks)
outcome_variable: Count of new building permits (filed and approved), multifamily vs single-family; units; medium-run listings and prices
outcome_standardization: Raw counts per block-quarter (not logged); effects expressed as % of control mean at boundary; Poisson in supply model to handle zeros.
treatment_definition_and_dose: Continuous dose via BAR: treatment = any increase in max BAR 2004->2016 map; IV per 1-unit increase in max BAR (28-63% more MF permits per unit BAR in manuscript).
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Reform effective 2016Q2; pre 2012Q2-2016Q1, post to 2019Q4; effect emerges ~1 year (two half-years) after reform; no pre-reform anticipation detected.
spillover_handling: Spatial DiD comparing all near-boundary blocks (treated+control) with 'pure control' blocks >0.5 km away; no evidence of reduced permitting in adjacent control blocks.
inference_method: SEs clustered by commuting zone (329); Conley SEs at 1/5/10/20 km as robustness.
robustness_checks: Polynomial order; optimal bandwidth; approved vs filed permits; single-family placebo (null); multiplicative-error and linear 2SLS (KP F) supply models.
data_construction_and_cleaning: ~30k residential permits 1997-2020 scraped from SMUL with address/zoning; zoning maps 2004 and 2016 digitised at block level (45,082/46,987 blocks matched, 96%); IPTU cadastre (3.3M units) collapsed to blocks; Properati and DataZap listings.
stated_limitations: Informal construction unobserved; enforcement/bribery possible; no pre-reform listings so no parallel-trend test for medium-run; demand IV exclusion concerns; no forward-looking households.

study: Büchler & Lutz (2024) JUE 143:103689, Canton of Zurich upzonings
comparison_design: Staggered event-study DiD (TWFE and Sun-Abraham interaction-weighted), last-treated as controls
comparison_group_definition: Last-treated rasters (upzoned 2015-2020) in other municipalities serve as controls for earlier cohorts; sample limited to rasters at least partly residential in 1995; downzoned or residential-to-other rezoned rasters dropped (4,208).
similarity_covariates: Controls: number of buildings in raster, changes in property-tax location categories on treated and neighbouring rasters. Descriptives show last-treated closer to CBD/transit and higher rent growth (argued to bias against findings). PS-weighted doubly robust estimator as robustness (App D.9; covariates only in appendix, not seen).
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Raster FE + period FE + controls; event-time dummies -15..+15 years (5-year bins), ref -5; Sun-Abraham to avoid negative weighting under heterogeneous effects; Callaway-Sant'Anna robustness.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Pre-period event coefficients; anticipation robustness (App D.6); comparison of early vs last-treated means (Table 2).
unit_of_analysis: 100 m x 100 m raster cell x 5-year period (1995-2020), 168 municipalities
outcome_variable: Housing units; living space (m2); hedonic rent; nominal rent per m2
outcome_standardization: Logs of units and floor space (zero handling not described in main text); hedonic rent from ~600k scraped listings.
treatment_definition_and_dose: Binary cohort indicator for upzoning = increase in allowed FAR; dose split at median FAR increase 30.7% (range 0-640%) into large vs small; bindingness = pre-period average floors vs maximum allowed floors.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Data aggregated to 5-year periods; cohort = period of upzoning (e.g., 1996-2000 -> 2000); rent heterogeneity uses cohorts from 2005 and split at median 2005 hedonic rent.
spillover_handling: Separate spillover regression on never-treated rasters with treated neighbours: dose = sum of FAR changes in adjacent rasters; controls = rasters with last-treated neighbours; rasters with neighbours treated at different times excluded.
robustness_checks: Callaway-Sant'Anna; lagged/no controls; exclude City of Zurich; alt FAR thresholds; MAUP (raster size); anticipation; balanced panel; changes-on-changes; PS-weighted doubly robust.
data_construction_and_cleaning: Zoning plans digitised by Statistical Office 1996-2020 and rasterised; Federal Register of Buildings and Dwellings (~850k units); web-scraped rents 2004-2020.
stated_limitations: No built FAR so bindingness proxied by floors; rent data only from 2004; Swiss institutional context.
where_in_paper: Sec 3.1-3.3, Sec 4.1 (eq 1), Sec 4.3 (spillovers), Sec 5.3 robustness, Online App D

study: Kulka, Sood & Chiumenti (2022) FRB Boston WP 22-10 / REStat 'Under the (Neighbor)Hood', Greater Boston
comparison_design: Cross-sectional boundary discontinuity at within-town regulation boundaries (lot level)
comparison_group_definition: Properties within 0.3 miles either side of 'admissible' regulation boundaries inside a single town AND school attendance area; boundaries intersecting highways, major roads, rivers/streams/lakes removed; 15 municipalities lacking attendance-zone data dropped (86 towns).
similarity_covariates: Amenity continuity: distance to water, town centre, highways, schools, open space regressed on boundary FE + distance bins; pre-1956 building-type composition as falsification. Price regressions deliberately exclude house characteristics (endogenous to regulation); indirect-effect spec adds unit characteristics.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Boundary-segment FE + linear distance function estimated separately each side + year FE; regulation indicators for scenario (DUPAC only, MF+DUPAC, height+DUPAC, etc.). Donut RD (exclude 0-0.1 mi) for neighbourhood-density spillovers.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Pre-1956 buildings show no type differences across present boundaries (Table 2); amenity-continuity plots (Fig 2).
unit_of_analysis: Residential building / lot (Warren Group assessor records 2010-2018)
outcome_variable: Units per building; LPM indicators for 2-3 unit and 4+ unit vs single-family; log owner cost; log rent
outcome_standardization: Units per building (levels) and % of mean; owner cost = 6.29% of assessed value; rents from CoStar (5+ units) or imputed via regression on CoStar/Warren/ACS.
treatment_definition_and_dose: Discrete regulation differences across boundary: multifamily allowed (0/1), max height, DUPAC (lots per acre after min lot size x max units per lot) - analysed by combination scenario.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Cross-sectional; supply samples restricted to buildings built after 1918 or 1956 (zoning milestones) to avoid grandfathered stock.
spillover_handling: Neighbourhood density (share of 2-3 and 4+ unit buildings within 0.1 mi) in donut RD for price externalities.
robustness_checks: Bandwidth 0.05-0.35 mi; year-built controls.
data_construction_and_cleaning: MAPC zoning atlas (lot-level regulations); Warren Group assessor; CoStar rents; NCES SABS 2016 school attendance boundaries; Chapter 40B locations. Code on GitHub (nchiumenti/boston_zoning).
stated_limitations: Direct effect includes option value and housing-type changes; cannot separate distaste for density from supply effects; zoning snapshot, little temporal variation; CoStar skews high end.
where_in_paper: Nov 2021 predecessor 'Local Barriers to Housing Density and Reducing Costs' (QMUL seminar version): Sec 3-5, eq 1-2 p20-21, Tables 1-5, Fig 7

study: Liao (2023) JMP, NYC rezonings (2004-2013)
comparison_design: Event-study DiD, upzoned areas vs adjacent buffer
comparison_group_definition: Parcels outside rezoning boundary within 1,000 ft (adjacent ring); parcels in any other rezoning (incl. downzonings/contextual) removed from control.
similarity_covariates: No matching; relies on proximity. Parcel/building characteristics (age, size, lot area) as controls; Table 3 shows baseline differences (treated lower max FAR 1.375 vs 1.755).
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Y_it = tract FE + rezoning-district FE + sub-borough-area x year FE + event-time dummies (-3..+7) x treated + X_it. SBA-year FE absorb local shocks; pooled 0-3 / 4-7 yr bins.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Event-study pre-coefficients flat; no formal balance test.
unit_of_analysis: Parcel x year (PLUTO 2002-2018)
outcome_variable: Residential units; sale prices; migration (Infutor)
outcome_standardization: Log(residential units per parcel) (zero handling not discussed); log price per unit (pre-2004 buildings; 2-yr bins).
treatment_definition_and_dose: Rezoning = upzoning if district-wide residential capacity (lot area x max residential FAR) rises >=20%; dose: no/moderate (<=50%)/substantial (>50%) parcel capacity increase.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Rezonings adopted 2004-2013, outcomes to 2018; effects significant only 2-3 yrs after; staggered timing handled with standard TWFE (no Sun-Abraham/CS).
spillover_handling: Rings 1,000-2,000 and 2,000-3,000 ft to test spillovers into controls: small, mostly insignificant positive; notes estimate could be lower or upper bound.
inference_method: SEs clustered by rezoning district; tract clustering as robustness.
robustness_checks: 10% capacity threshold; 500-ft narrow band for prices; heterogeneity central vs peripheral, rent-stabilised.
data_construction_and_cleaning: PLUTO annual vintages, DCP rezoning shapefiles, DOB permits, DOF/ACRIS sales, Infutor address histories with BIFSG race imputation; tenure imputed by building type. Lot splits/merges not explicitly handled.
stated_limitations: Hyper-local, not general equilibrium; only large (>=20%) rezonings often bundled with infrastructure; boundaries possibly endogenous; no rent data.
where_in_paper: Sec 3-5 (p14-22), eq 1 p19, Table 3-4, Sec 6.1 p33, App C

study: Freemark, Su & Curran-Groome (2026) Urban Institute, NYC and Philadelphia upzonings
comparison_design: Matching (generalized full matching) + event-study DiD; Sun-Abraham for staggered NYC
comparison_group_definition: NYC: parcels in same borough not upzoned or downzoned, matched to ~3,600 upzoned parcels; downzoned excluded. Philadelphia: block faces with no increase in zoning envelope citywide (downzoned retained; sensitivity drops top-decile decreases).
similarity_covariates: NYC: exact match on categorised pre-treatment residential-unit change, unit counts in each of 6 pre-years, whether residential allowed pre-upzoning; inexact on improvement/land value ratio. Philadelphia: median HH income, median rent, racial composition, tree cover, pre-reform zoning capacity, pre-treatment units and unit change.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: MatchIt 'fast generalized full matching' weights, then event-study with unit (parcel/block face) FE and year FE; Sun-Abraham for staggered NYC cohorts.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Standardised mean differences <=0.1 after matching (Fig B1); flat pre-period event coefficients.
unit_of_analysis: NYC parcel x year (2010-2023); Philadelphia block face x year (2005-2024)
outcome_variable: NYC: residential units on parcel (PLUTO, completed stock); Philadelphia: permit applications and units proposed
outcome_standardization: Levels: units per parcel / units per block face per year; aggregated to city totals.
treatment_definition_and_dose: NYC: upzoned if permitted FAR up >0.25 within 7 neighbourhood rezonings (2016-2021); robustness with modelled zoning envelope. Philadelphia: capacity (FAR, height, coverage, setbacks, parking) pre vs post 2012 code.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: Reference year = year before upzoning; Philadelphia pre 2005-2011, post 2012-2024; remapping delayed (56% of acres not remapped by 2017); significant effects after ~6 yrs.
spillover_handling: Not tested; acknowledged; block-face aggregation partly absorbs parcel-to-parcel spillovers.
inference_method: 95% CIs; SEs clustered by parcel/block face.
robustness_checks: Envelope vs FAR treatment; excluding strongly downzoned block faces.
data_construction_and_cleaning: PLUTO; Philadelphia L&I permits; capacity modelled per parcel.
stated_limitations: Cannot separate upzoning from concurrent public investments; Gowanus industrial conversion; permits vs completions in Philadelphia; no year-by-year zoning in Philadelphia.
where_in_paper: Report pp. 8-17, 25-34, App B (Fig B1)

study: Freemark (2020) Urban Affairs Review 56(3), Chicago TOD upzoning
comparison_design: DiD with later-treated and never-treated comparison groups
comparison_group_definition: Primary: parcels upzoned by 2015 TOD expansion (same zoning classes, slightly further from stations) as controls for 2013 reform parcels; secondary: 'outside' parcels within 1/2 mile of stations that would have qualified but not on Pedestrian Streets.
similarity_covariates: Property: distance to station, land sq ft, assessor property type, underlying zoning class/density, neighbourhood building coverage; tract: population density, ethnicity, transit use, education, income, house values.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Covariate regression with district FE and quarter FE (prices) or year FE (permits); some models add district linear trends.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Covariate summaries show similarity between 2013 and 2015 groups; loess price trends aligned at law date; formal test -1000..-500 vs -500..0 days no difference; placebo dates every day.
unit_of_analysis: Transaction (prices); planning district x year (permits)
outcome_variable: Log sale price; count of new residential units permitted
outcome_standardization: Log prices; unit counts (levels); transactions <$500 dropped.
treatment_definition_and_dose: Binary eligibility by reform (2013: FAR up to 3.5, +33-50% units, 50% parking cut; 2015: FAR up to 4, no parking); separate density vs parking-only classes.
time_alignment_and_anticipation: 2013 ordinance Sept 2013; window -1000 to +744 days; anticipation sensitivity via proposal dates.
spillover_handling: Not modelled; buffer-zone subsamples at edge of 2013/2015 areas.
inference_method: Robust SEs clustered by census tract.
robustness_checks: Buffer zones; daily placebo dates; shorter windows; ward controls.
data_construction_and_cleaning: IL Dept of Revenue sales 2010-2018 (no unit size); Chicago permits geocoded, deduplicated, units parsed from free-text; 2012 zoning.
stated_limitations: One city in weak market period; no nonresidential scale data; rentals not measured; author advocated for the reform.

study: Stacy, Davis, Freemark, Lo, MacDonald, Zheng & Pendall (2023) Land-use reforms and housing costs (Urban Institute report version of Urban Studies article)
comparison_design: Panel fixed-effects regression with staggered reform timing (generalized DiD / event windows) plus falsification leads
comparison_group_definition: Cities in the same 8 metros (Boston, Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Los Angeles, Miami, Philadelphia, Portland) with no reform found in newspapers; authors concede controls may include unmeasured treated cities (attenuation). Reformers were far larger at baseline (mean 2000 pop ~190-212k vs ~19.7k for non-reformers, Table 3).
similarity_covariates: No matching/weighting on covariates. Similarity imposed only via city FE, period FE, city-specific linear trends and 'controls for regional context'.
how_similarity_enters_estimation: City FE (lambda_i) + quarter or year FE (theta_t) + city-specific linear time trends (varsigma_i*t). Separate indicators for restrictive vs loosening reforms in an Implementation window and a Post window. No propensity score, SC or reweighting.
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Figure 2 raw trends (both reform types had rising unit counts pre-reform); falsification test with hypothetical future reforms 3 yrs before: no pre-effect on address counts, but loosening cities had falling aggregate rents before reform (Tables 6-7) = some endogeneity in rents. No covariate balance table beyond Table 3 descriptives.
unit_of_analysis: City (place)-quarter for USPS addresses (1,136 cities, 2005Q4-2021Q1); city-year for ACS rent outcomes (2008-2017 panel)
outcome_variable: (1) USPS total residential address count; (2) median gross rent and aggregate gross rent (ACS 5-yr); (3) count of rental units affordable at ELI/VLI/LI/MI/above bands (30%-of-income rule, national median income; AMI in robustness)
outcome_standardization: Natural log of counts when variable and residuals are log-distributed (fn 2) -> semi-elasticities; rents in dollars; affordability band counts logged and interpolated within rent buckets. study: Westreich, Edwards, Lesko, Stuart & Cole (2017) Am J Epidemiol 186(8):1010-1014, Transportability of trial results using inverse odds of sampling weights
comparison_design: Methods paper: transport an effect estimated in a study sample (S=1) to a separate, possibly non-overlapping, target population (S=0)
comparison_group_definition: Target population described by covariate data only (no outcomes needed)
similarity_covariates: Z must be 'S-admissible': pretreatment covariates that d-separate sampling from outcome, i.e. effect modifiers whose distribution differs between sample and target
how_similarity_enters_estimation: Stack sample and target; fit logistic P(S=1|Z); weight sample units by W=[P(S=0|Z)/P(S=1|Z)]x[P(S=1)/P(S=0)], target rows weight 0; fit outcome/effect model on weighted sample. Unlike IPSW (sample nested in target), IOSW allows disjoint populations and is invariant to target size
pretreatment_fit_or_balance_checks: Paper stresses positivity (P(S=1|Z=z)>0 across target); little else on diagnostics in what I read. Related Stuart et al. 2011/2015 work recommends comparing mean propensity score between sample and target and checking covariate balance after weighting (not read here: Springer page was rate-limited)
